    53  def jsonWithTheoremFalse (chunks : List ByteArray) : Prop :=
    54    ∃ (before between₁ between₂ between₃ after name : String) (i j k v : Nat),

    61  {between₃}

== ConLeche/Model/StreamConsts.lean#L84-L90
    84  @[expose] def Declaration.Declares : Declaration → ConstantVal → Prop
    85    | .defnDecl cv _ _, cv' => cv' = cv
    86    | .thmDecl cv _, cv' => cv' = cv
    87    | .opaqueDecl cv _, cv' => cv' = cv
    88    | .axiomDecl cv, cv' => cv' = cv ∧ cv.name ≠ sorryAxName ∧ cv.name ≠ quotSoundName
    89    | .indDecl _ _, _ => False
    90    | .quotDecl _ _, _ => False

== ConLeche/Kernel/Install.lean#L79-L91
    79  def declConstants : Declaration → List ConstantInfo
    80    | .defnDecl cv value hint => [.defnInfo cv value hint]
    81    | .thmDecl cv _ => [.thmInfo cv]
    82    | .opaqueDecl cv _ => [.axiomInfo cv]
    83    | .axiomDecl cv =>
    84      if cv.name = quotSoundName then [quotAt .sound cv]
    85      else if cv.name = sorryAxName then []
    86      else [.axiomInfo cv]
    87    | .quotDecl k cv => [quotAt k cv]
    88    | .indDecl block nP =>
    89      match readBlock nP block with
    90      | .ok p => blockConstants p
    91      | .error _ => []

   707      whnfCoreI mode fe₁ = whnfCoreI mode fe₂ ∧ whnfI mode fe₁ = whnfI mode fe₂ ∧

== ConLeche/Kernel/TypeChecker.lean#L29-L54
    29  def whnfCore (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) (cheap : Bool := false) :
    30      CheckM Expr :=
    31    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).whnfCore cheap depth e
    32  
    33  /-- The full reduction loop (fueled). -/
    34  def whnf (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) : CheckM Expr :=
    35    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).whnf depth e
    36  
    37  /-- Full-grade type inference (fueled): the declaration front door's
    38  entry — official's `infer_type_core(e, infer_only = false)`. -/
    39  def inferTypeCore (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) : CheckM Expr :=
    40    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).infer depth e
    41  
    42  /-- Type inference at the io grade (fueled): the knot's `inferIO` slot
    43  — what every internal inference call site runs (task #170).  At every
    44  mode it is the io lane (`inferTypeIO_on`, `Verify/Knot.lean`). -/
    45  def inferTypeIO (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) : CheckM Expr :=
    46    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).inferIO depth e
    47  
    48  /-- Definitional equality (fueled). -/
    49  def isDefEqCore (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (a b : Expr) : CheckM Bool :=
    50    (pureFns mode eager env fuel).defeq depth a b
    51  
    52  /-- `ensureSort` over the pure knot (fueled). -/
    53  def ensureSortCore (env : Env) (fuel depth : Nat) (e : Expr) : CheckM Level :=
    54    ensureSort (pureFns mode eager env fuel) env depth e

== ConLeche/Kernel/Core.lean#L1866-L1884
  1866  def defeqBody (eager : Bool) (r : CoreFns m) (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → Expr → m Bool :=
  1867    fun depth a b => do
  1868      if a == b then pure true else
  1869      match ctorTargetFor env eager a b with
  1870      | some c =>
  1871        let w ← r.whnf depth a
  1872        match ctorHeadAgainst env c w with
  1873        | some true => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth w b
  1874        | some false => pure false
  1875        | none => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth a b
  1876      | none =>
  1877      match ctorTargetFor env eager b a with
  1878      | some c =>
  1879        let w ← r.whnf depth b
  1880        match ctorHeadAgainst env c w with
  1881        | some true => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth a w
  1882        | some false => pure false
  1883        | none => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth a b
  1884      | none => defeqLazy mode eager r env depth a b

== ConLeche/Kernel/Exclusive.lean#L6-L42
     6  # `withExclusive`: the reference-count read behind the walk memo
     7  
     8  **What it is.**  `withExclusive a k h` runs the continuation `k` on
     9  whether the object `a` is *exclusive* — single-threaded with reference
    10  count exactly 1, so that no other reference to it exists.  In the logic
    11  it is `k false` ("not known to be exclusive", the conservative answer);
    12  in compiled code `@[implemented_by]` substitutes `k
    13  (isExclusiveUnsafe a)`, the real count read off the object header
    14  (`Init/Util.lean`, `@[extern "lean_is_exclusive_obj"]`, a BORROWED
    15  parameter; `lean_is_exclusive` in `lean.h`).  A multi-threaded object
    16  (count `< 0`) and a persistent one (count `0` — the installed
    17  environment after the driver's `Runtime.markPersistent`) answer
    18  `false`, which is the safe side.
    19  
    20  **What justifies the substitution** is the obligation
    21  
    22  ```
    23  h : k true = k false
    24  ```
    25  
    26  — the continuation's value does not depend on the answer, so the
    27  compiled program computes the very value the definition names.  A
    28  caller may use the answer to choose *how* to compute a value, never
    29  *which* value.  `Init.Util`'s `withPtrAddr` is the same arrangement
    30  (`k 0` in the model, the address in the binary, the continuation
    31  address-blind by obligation), and `Bool` being two-valued makes
    32  `k true = k false` the whole of `∀ b₁ b₂, k b₁ = k b₂`.
    33  
    34  **What it is for.**  The per-walk memo tables of the substitution walks
    35  (`ConLeche/Cached/ExprOpsC.lean`) exist for one reason: a node reached
    36  twice — a shared sub-DAG — must be rebuilt once, so that the walk is
    37  `O(DAG)` and its OUTPUT stays shared.  A node with exactly one
    38  reference cannot be reached twice, so recording it is pure loss: the
    39  key, the entry, the probe.  The official kernel's `replace_fn`
    40  (`src/kernel/replace_fn.cpp`) therefore caches a node's replacement
    41  only when `!is_likely_unshared(e)` — the same read.  The walks memoise
    42  exactly the nodes this primitive reports shared.

== ConLeche/Term/Syntax.lean#L188-L219
   188  inductive Term where
   189    /-- de Bruijn index -/
   190    | bvar (i : Nat)
   191    /-- `Sort u` at a concrete level -/
   192    | sort (u : Nat)
   193    /-- a built-in constant at a concrete level instantiation -/
   194    | const (c : BConst) (us : List Nat)
   195    /-- application -/
   196    | app (f a : Term)
   197    /-- `fun (_ : ty) => body` -/
   198    | lam (ty body : Term)
   199    /-- `(_ : ty) → body` -/
   200    | pi (ty body : Term)
   201    /-- `let _ := val; body`, **without the type**: the body is under one
   202    binder, read at the value -/
   203    | letE (val body : Term)
   204    /-- `@Eq _ lhs rhs`, **without the type**: the interpretation is
   205    `⟦eqE a b⟧ = eqv ⟦a⟧ ⟦b⟧`, so soundness never constrains the type,
   206    and no definition and no theorem in any tier reads the type, so
   207    the constructor does not carry it; a producer that knows the type
   208    simply drops it. -/
   209    | eqE (lhs rhs : Term)
   210    /-- First field of a pair.  Carries **only** the subject: the pair's
   211    type arguments come from the typing premise `Γ ⊢ p : Σ A B`,
   212    not from the term — see the module docstring.  Interpreted by
   213    `sfst`, i.e. literally `interp`'s clause. -/
   214    | fst (e : Term)
   215    /-- Second field of a pair; the `fst` twin, interpreted by `ssnd`. -/
   216    | snd (e : Term)
   217    /-- the canonical (irrelevant) proof of a derivable equation -/
   218    | prf
   219    deriving Repr, Inhabited

== ConLeche/Semantics/Interp.lean#L291-L292
   291  noncomputable def interp (ρ : Nat → V) (t : Term) : V :=
   292    (interpDef V ρ 0 t).val Fin.elim0

== ConLeche/Semantics/WellDenoted.lean#L49-L72
    49  def WellDenoted : (Nat → V) → Term → Prop
    50    | ρ, .pi A B =>
    51      WellDenoted ρ A ∧ IsTy (interp V ρ A) ∧
    52      (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp V ρ A → WellDenoted (cons x ρ) B) ∧
    53      (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp V ρ A → IsTy (interp V (cons x ρ) B))
    54    | ρ, .lam A b =>
    55      WellDenoted ρ A ∧ IsTy (interp V ρ A) ∧
    56      (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp V ρ A → WellDenoted (cons x ρ) b)
    57    | ρ, .app f a =>
    58      WellDenoted ρ f ∧ WellDenoted ρ a ∧ AppliesTo (interp V ρ f) (interp V ρ a)
    59    | ρ, .fst e =>
    60      WellDenoted ρ e ∧
    61      ∃ u v A Bf, ∃ hS : HasSigmaPairs A Bf, interp V ρ e ∈ˢ sigmaSet (Nat.max u v) A Bf hS ∧
    62        A ∈ˢ univ u ∧ ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → Bf x ∈ˢ univ v
    63    | ρ, .snd e =>
    64      WellDenoted ρ e ∧
    65      ∃ u v A Bf, ∃ hS : HasSigmaPairs A Bf, interp V ρ e ∈ˢ sigmaSet (Nat.max u v) A Bf hS ∧
    66        A ∈ˢ univ u ∧ ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → Bf x ∈ˢ univ v
    67    | ρ, .eqE a b => WellDenoted ρ a ∧ WellDenoted ρ b
    68    | ρ, .letE v b => WellDenoted ρ v ∧ WellDenoted (cons (interp V ρ v) ρ) b
    69    | _, .bvar _ => True
    70    | _, .sort _ => True
    71    | _, .const _ _ => True
    72    | _, .prf => True

== ConLeche/Semantics/WellDenoted.lean#L125-L291
   125  /-! ### The substitution metatheory -/
   126  
   127  /-- Truthfulness through lifting. -/
   128  theorem WellDenoted_liftN (n : Nat) :
   129      ∀ (e : Term) (k : Nat) (ρ : Nat → V),
   130        WellDenoted V ρ (e.liftN n k) ↔ WellDenoted V (shiftE n k ρ) e := by
   131    intro e
   132    induction e with
   133    | bvar i =>
   134      intro k ρ
   135      simp only [Term.liftN_bvar]
   136      split <;> simp
   137    | sort u => intro k ρ; simp
   138    | const c us => intro k ρ; simp
   139    | app f a ihf iha =>
   140      intro k ρ
   141      rw [Term.liftN_app, WellDenoted_app, WellDenoted_app, ihf, iha,
   142        interp_liftN, interp_liftN]
   143    | lam A b ihA ihb =>
   144      intro k ρ
   145      rw [Term.liftN_lam, WellDenoted_lam, WellDenoted_lam, ihA, interp_liftN]
   146      refine and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr Iff.rfl
   147        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_))
   148      rw [ihb, cons_shiftE]
   149    | pi A B ihA ihB =>
   150      intro k ρ
   151      rw [Term.liftN_pi, WellDenoted_pi, WellDenoted_pi, ihA, interp_liftN]
   152      refine and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr
   153        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_)
   154        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_)))
   155      · rw [ihB, cons_shiftE]
   156      · rw [interp_liftN, cons_shiftE]
   157    | letE v b ihv ihb =>
   158      intro k ρ
   159      rw [Term.liftN_letE, WellDenoted_letE, WellDenoted_letE, ihv,
   160        interp_liftN, ihb, cons_shiftE]
   161    | eqE a b iha ihb =>
   162      intro k ρ
   163      rw [Term.liftN_eqE, WellDenoted_eqE, WellDenoted_eqE, iha, ihb]
   164    | fst e ihe =>
   165      intro k ρ
   166      rw [Term.liftN_fst, WellDenoted_fst, WellDenoted_fst, ihe,
   167        interp_liftN]
   168    | snd e ihe =>
   169      intro k ρ
   170      rw [Term.liftN_snd, WellDenoted_snd, WellDenoted_snd, ihe,
   171        interp_liftN]
   172    | prf => intro k ρ; simp
   173  
   174  /-- Truthfulness through instantiation. -/
   175  theorem WellDenoted_inst :
   176      ∀ (e a : Term) (k : Nat) (ρ : Nat → V),
   177        WellDenoted V (shiftE k 0 ρ) a →
   178        (WellDenoted V ρ (e.inst a k) ↔
   179          WellDenoted V (instE k (interp V (shiftE k 0 ρ) a) ρ) e) := by
   180    intro e
   181    induction e with
   182    | bvar i =>
   183      intro a k ρ ha
   184      show WellDenoted V ρ
   185          (if i < k then .bvar i
   186           else if i = k then Term.liftN k a else .bvar (i - 1)) ↔ _
   187      by_cases h : i < k
   188      · simp [ite_eq_left h]
   189      · by_cases h2 : i = k
   190        · simp only [ite_eq_right h, ite_eq_left h2, WellDenoted_bvar, iff_true]
   191          exact (WellDenoted_liftN V k a 0 ρ).mpr ha
   192        · simp [ite_eq_right h, ite_eq_right h2]
   193    | sort u => intro a k ρ _; simp [Term.inst]
   194    | const c us => intro a k ρ _; simp [Term.inst]
   195    | app f b ihf ihb =>
   196      intro a k ρ ha
   197      rw [Term.inst_app, WellDenoted_app, WellDenoted_app, ihf a k ρ ha,
   198        ihb a k ρ ha, interp_inst, interp_inst]
   199    | lam A b ihA ihb =>
   200      intro a k ρ ha
   201      rw [Term.inst_lam, WellDenoted_lam, WellDenoted_lam, ihA a k ρ ha,
   202        interp_inst]
   203      refine and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr Iff.rfl
   204        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_))
   205      have ha' : WellDenoted V (shiftE (k + 1) 0 (cons x ρ)) a := by
   206        rw [shiftE_succ_cons]; exact ha
   207      rw [ihb a (k + 1) (cons x ρ) ha', shiftE_succ_cons, cons_instE]
   208    | pi A B ihA ihB =>
   209      intro a k ρ ha
   210      rw [Term.inst_pi, WellDenoted_pi, WellDenoted_pi, ihA a k ρ ha,
   211        interp_inst]
   212      refine and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr Iff.rfl (and_congr
   213        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_)
   214        (forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr Iff.rfl ?_)))
   215      · have ha' : WellDenoted V (shiftE (k + 1) 0 (cons x ρ)) a := by
   216          rw [shiftE_succ_cons]; exact ha
   217        rw [ihB a (k + 1) (cons x ρ) ha', shiftE_succ_cons, cons_instE]
   218      · rw [interp_inst, shiftE_succ_cons, cons_instE]
   219    | letE v b ihv ihb =>
   220      intro a k ρ ha
   221      rw [Term.inst_letE, WellDenoted_letE, WellDenoted_letE, ihv a k ρ ha,
   222        interp_inst]
   223      refine and_congr Iff.rfl ?_
   224      have ha' : WellDenoted V (shiftE (k + 1) 0
   225          (cons (interp V (instE k (interp V (shiftE k 0 ρ) a) ρ) v) ρ)) a := by
   226        rw [shiftE_succ_cons]; exact ha
   227      rw [ihb a (k + 1) _ ha', shiftE_succ_cons, cons_instE]
   228    | eqE x y ihx ihy =>
   229      intro a k ρ ha
   230      rw [Term.inst_eqE, WellDenoted_eqE, WellDenoted_eqE, ihx a k ρ ha,
   231        ihy a k ρ ha]
   232    | fst e ihe =>
   233      intro a k ρ ha
   234      rw [Term.inst_fst, WellDenoted_fst, WellDenoted_fst, ihe a k ρ ha,
   235        interp_inst]
   236    | snd e ihe =>
   237      intro a k ρ ha
   238      rw [Term.inst_snd, WellDenoted_snd, WellDenoted_snd, ihe a k ρ ha,
   239        interp_inst]
   240    | prf => intro a k ρ _; simp [Term.inst]
   241  
   242  /-- Substitution at the outermost binder — the β/ζ transport form. -/
   243  theorem WellDenoted_inst0 {e a : Term} {ρ : Nat → V}
   244      (ha : WellDenoted V ρ a) :
   245      WellDenoted V ρ (e.inst a) ↔
   246        WellDenoted V (cons (interp V ρ a) ρ) e := by
   247    have h := WellDenoted_inst V e a 0 ρ (by rwa [shiftE_zero_zero])
   248    rwa [shiftE_zero_zero, instE_zero] at h
   249  
   250  /-- **ζ, graded**: a `let` interprets as its reduct, and with its value
   251  graded it is graded exactly when its reduct is.  Unconditional: no
   252  binder, so no regime. -/
   253  theorem interp_zeta (v b : Term) (ρ : Nat → V) :
   254      interp V ρ (.letE v b) = interp V ρ (b.inst v) := by
   255    rw [interp_letE, interp_inst0]
   256  
   257  theorem WellDenoted_zeta {v b : Term} {ρ : Nat → V}
   258      (hv : WellDenoted V ρ v) :
   259      WellDenoted V ρ (.letE v b) ↔ WellDenoted V ρ (b.inst v) := by
   260    rw [WellDenoted_letE, WellDenoted_inst0 V hv]
   261    exact and_iff_right hv
   262  
   263  /-! ### The graded β step
   264  
   265  At a redex that is not the point, from the subject's `WellDenoted`
   266  alone: the λ is not the point (`app_pt`), so it is a graph and the
   267  application clause reads the argument off the graph: it lies in the
   268  λ's domain (`appliesTo_graph`), and β is `app_lamV`.  At the point there
   269  is nothing to show: the claims that read this are conditional on "not
   270  the point". -/
   271  
   272  /-- **The graded β step** at a redex that is not the point. -/
   273  theorem WellDenoted_beta {A b a : Term} {ρ : Nat → V}
   274      (h : WellDenoted V ρ (.app (.lam A b) a))
   275      (hne : interp V ρ (.app (.lam A b) a) ≠ pt) :
   276      interp V ρ a ∈ˢ interp V ρ A ∧
   277      interp V ρ (.app (.lam A b) a) = interp V ρ (b.inst a) ∧
   278      WellDenoted V ρ (b.inst a) := by
   279    rw [WellDenoted_app] at h
   280    obtain ⟨hlam, ha, hap⟩ := h
   281    have hlne : interp V ρ (.lam A b) ≠ pt := by
   282      intro h0; apply hne; rw [interp_app, h0, app_pt]
   283    obtain ⟨-, -, hbody⟩ := (WellDenoted_lam V ρ A b).mp hlam
   284    have hgraph : interp V ρ (.lam A b) =
   285        graph (fun x => interp V (cons x ρ) b) (interp V ρ A)
   286          (interp_hasGraph_cons ρ (interp V ρ A) b) := by
   287      rw [interp_lam] at hlne ⊢; exact lamV_eq_graph hlne
   288    have haA : interp V ρ a ∈ˢ interp V ρ A := by
   289      rw [hgraph] at hap; exact (appliesTo_graph.mp hap).2
   290    refine ⟨haA, ?_, (WellDenoted_inst0 V ha).mpr (hbody _ haA)⟩
   291    rw [interp_app, interp_lam, app_lamV haA, interp_inst0]

== ConLeche/Model/Env/EnvModel.lean#L35-L63
    35  structure EnvModel (env : Env) where
    36    /-- the shared, model-free environment well-formedness -/
    37    wf : EnvWF env
    38    /-- the leaf valuation: each constant's reading at a level assignment -/
    39    acval : Name → (Name → Nat) → Term
    40    /-- every leaf is closed -/
    41    cval_closed : ∀ (n : Name) (ψ : Name → Nat),
    42      Term.Closed (acval n ψ)
    43    /-- the reserved basis constants are the pinned declarations, valued
    44    by their direct pins (V-free) -/
    45    basis_pinned : BasisPinnedTT env acval
    46    /-- every stored native projection-table entry is a pinned pair
    47    entry with its block stored (V-free, shared) -/
    48    proj_ok : ProjOkT env
    49    /-- every stored recursor rule's constructor is stored (V-free,
    50    shared) -/
    51    rec_ctors : RecCtorsStored env
    52    /-- a leaf reads only its own level parameters -/
    53    acval_params : ∀ (n : Name) (ci : ConstantInfo),
    54      env.find? n = some ci →
    55      ∀ ψ₁ ψ₂ : Name → Nat,
    56        (∀ p ∈ ci.toConstantVal.levelParams, ψ₁ p = ψ₂ p) →
    57        acval n ψ₁ = acval n ψ₂
    58    /-- every leaf is truthful -/
    59    acval_wellDenoted : ∀ (n : Name) (ψ : Name → Nat) (ρ : Nat → V),
    60      WellDenoted V ρ (acval n ψ)

   194  theorem Denotes_of_denote {acval : Name → (Name → Nat) → Term}
   195      (hcl : ∀ n ψ, Term.Closed (acval n ψ)) {env : Env} {φ : Name → Nat} :

   199        ∀ ρ : Nat → V,
   200          Denotes (cvalOf (V := V) acval) env φ ρ (closeN d e) (interp V ρ ta) := by

== ConLeche/Model/Claims.lean#L49-L125
    49  /-- Head normalisation, dual success, P currency, conditional on the
    50  point (task #342, L9): the reduct is graded and equal where the subject
    51  is not the point. -/
    52  @[expose] def WhnfCoreClaim {env : Env} (m : EnvModel V env)
    53      (φ : Name → Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Prop :=
    54    ∀ {d : Nat} {e e' : Expr} {Δa : List Term},
    55      whnfCore .verified false env fuel d e = .ok e' →
    56      Expr.WScoped d e → e.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
    57      Expr.LeavesBounded e →
    58      ∀ {ea ea' : Term},
    59        CtxOk m φ d Δa e →
    60        denote m.acval env φ d e = some ea →
    61        denote m.acval env φ d e' = some ea' →
    62        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ ea) →
    63        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → interp V ρ ea ≠ pt →
    64            WellDenoted V ρ ea') ∧
    65          ∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → interp V ρ ea ≠ pt →
    66            interp V ρ ea = interp V ρ ea'
    67  
    68  /-- The reduction loop, dual success, P currency, conditional on the
    69  point (task #342, L9). -/
    70  @[expose] def WhnfClaim {env : Env} (m : EnvModel V env)
    71      (φ : Name → Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Prop :=
    72    ∀ {d : Nat} {e e' : Expr} {Δa : List Term},
    73      whnf .verified false env fuel d e = .ok e' →
    74      Expr.WScoped d e → e.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
    75      Expr.LeavesBounded e →
    76      ∀ {ea ea' : Term},
    77        CtxOk m φ d Δa e →
    78        denote m.acval env φ d e = some ea →
    79        denote m.acval env φ d e' = some ea' →
    80        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ ea) →
    81        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → interp V ρ ea ≠ pt →
    82            WellDenoted V ρ ea') ∧
    83          ∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → interp V ρ ea ≠ pt →
    84            interp V ρ ea = interp V ρ ea'
    85  
    86  /-- Definitional equality, P currency, conditional on the point (task
    87  #342, L9): two sides that are not the point are equal.  A consumer
    88  comparing two types or two members of one type closes with
    89  `eq_of_IsTy_of_ne_pt` / `IsTy.eq_of_ne_pt`. -/
    90  @[expose] def DefEqClaim {env : Env} (m : EnvModel V env)
    91      (φ : Name → Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Prop :=
    92    ∀ {d : Nat} {a b : Expr} {Δa : List Term},
    93      ConLeche.isDefEqCore .verified false env fuel d a b = .ok true →
    94      Expr.WScoped d a → a.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
    95      Expr.LeavesBounded a →
    96      Expr.WScoped d b → b.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
    97      Expr.LeavesBounded b →
    98      ∀ {aa ba : Term},
    99        CtxOk m φ d Δa a →
   100        CtxOk m φ d Δa b →
   101        denote m.acval env φ d a = some aa →
   102        denote m.acval env φ d b = some ba →
   103        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ aa) →
   104        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ ba) →
   105        ∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ →
   106          interp V ρ aa ≠ pt → interp V ρ ba ≠ pt →
   107          interp V ρ aa = interp V ρ ba
   108  
   109  /-- Inference, dual success, P currency: the subject's and the
   110  type's truthfulness are *conclusions*, and
   111  the type denotes a type. -/
   112  @[expose] def InferClaim {env : Env} (m : EnvModel V env)
   113      (φ : Name → Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Prop :=
   114    ∀ {d : Nat} {e t : Expr} {Δa : List Term},
   115      inferTypeCore .verified false env fuel d e = .ok t →
   116      Expr.WScoped d e → e.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
   117      Expr.LeavesBounded e →
   118      ∀ {ea ta : Term},
   119        CtxOk m φ d Δa e →
   120        denote m.acval env φ d e = some ea →
   121        denote m.acval env φ d t = some ta →
   122        (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenoted V ρ ea) ∧
   123          (∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ → WellDenotedTy V ρ ta) ∧
   124          ∀ ρ : Nat → V, Sat V Δa ρ →
   125            interp V ρ ea ∈ˢ interp V ρ ta

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L103-L107
   103  
   104  /-- **Reduction**: the head steps of `whnfCore` and the `whnf` loop,
   105  chained. -/
   106  inductive Red (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   107    /-- Every `pure e` exit: the value clauses of `whnfCoreBody`

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L329-L352
   329  checker only ever compares terms that are well-formed *together* — a
   330  fact the rules never state, because well-formedness (scoping, the
   331  readability of the terms, the grading of the reading) is semantic
   332  and may not enter this inductive.  Every rule respects one syntactic
   333  discipline instead: **the subject of each `DefEq` premise is either a
   334  subterm of the conclusion or is produced by an existence-form `Red` /
   335  `Infer` premise** (a reduct, an inferred type), so the soundness proof
   336  (`ConLeche/Model/Rules/Sound.lean`) always has the premise's terms in
   337  hand.  `trans` is the unique rule that would break it: its middle
   338  term comes from nowhere, and with it two rules that are each sound
   339  alone meet — `fvar` compares free variables by index only (their
   340  types are not compared, as the checker does not), while
   341  `proofFast` *reads* a head's stored data to decide "definitely a
   342  proof" — and derive `DefEq env d (.fvar i ty) (.fvar i' ty')` for
   343  every `i`, `i'`, which no model satisfies.  The recursive-structure rules
   344  (`redL`, `natSucc`, `eta`, `structUnit`) are therefore not a
   345  proof-engineering convenience but what keeps the relation sound; the
   346  one chaining that is sound, "reduce, then continue", is `redL`, and
   347  its right-hand and δ variants are derived in `Derived.lean`. -/
   348  inductive DefEq (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   349    /-- The syntactic fast paths (`defeqBody`, `quickDefEq`),
   350    the literal leaf (`:1582`), a same-index `fvar` pair is `fvar`
   351    below. -/
   352    | refl {d : Nat} {a : Expr} : DefEq env d a a

== ConLeche/Kernel/CoreDefs.lean#L458-L466
   458  /-- The certified structural-`Nat` operations.  Six of them
   459  (`add sub mul pow beq ble`) carry a literal fast path; `Nat.pred` is
   460  here without one — it has no fast path (official's `reduce_nat` folds
   461  nothing unary but `Nat.succ`), but `Nat.sub`'s recurrence
   462  `sub x (succ y) = pred (sub x y)` names it, so its own recurrences
   463  must be certified for `sub`'s literal fold to be sound. -/
   464  def natOpNames : List Name :=
   465    [natPredName, natAddName, natSubName, natMulName, natPowName,
   466     natBeqName, natBleName]

== ConLeche/Kernel/CoreDefs.lean#L391-L408
   391    else if c.name = listNilName then listNilTyOk (some c)
   392    else if c.name = listConsName then listConsTyOk (some c)
   393    else if c.name = charName then charTyOk (some c)
   394    else if c.name = charOfNatName then charOfNatTyOk (some c)
   395    else true
   396  
   397  /-! ## Structural-Nat literal acceleration
   398  
   399  The official kernel accelerates the structural `Nat` operations on
   400  literals (GMP-backed there).  Here the fast path is *certified*: an
   401  operation participates only when its defining recurrence equations
   402  hold by definitional equality — checked once, at its check: `checkDecl`
   403  positively rejects a nonstandard definition under one of these names,
   404  so *presence in the store is the certificate* (no runtime flag, no
   405  re-checking; a reduction-time re-check would in fact livelock — the
   406  certification's own `pred zero` equation re-enters the fast path).
   407  
   408  The certification runs in the environment *before* the operation is

   106      List (Expr × Expr) → m Bool
   107    | [] => pure true
   108    | eq :: rest => do
   109      if ← ops.isDefEq env 2 eq.1 eq.2 then
   110        certifyNatEqs ops env rest
   111      else pure false

== ConLeche/Model/DivModCert.lean#L1961

== ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean#L227-L240
   227  compute.  `a ^ b` has at most `natSizeBytes a * b` bytes, and a base
   228  `≤ 1` gives `0` or `1`; `a <<< b` has about `natSizeBytes a + b / 8`
   229  bytes, and `0 <<< b = 0`. -/
   230  def natOpRefusal (maxNatSize : Nat) (op : NatBinOp) (a b : Nat) : Option CheckError :=
   231    match op with
   232    | .pow =>
   233      if b > natCountMax then some (natCountTooBig "Nat.pow")
   234      else if a > 1 && b != 0 && natSizeBytes a > maxNatSize / b then
   235        some (.invalid "the kernel refused to evaluate `Nat.pow` because the result would \
   236          exceed the maximum numeral size; raise it with --max-nat-size")
   237      else none
   238    | .shiftLeft =>
   239      if a = 0 then none
   240      else if b > natCountMax then some (natCountTooBig "Nat.shiftLeft")

== ConLeche/Kernel/CoreDefs.lean#L589-L609
   589  def natOpResult (c : Name) (a b : Nat) : Option Expr :=
   590    if c = natPredName then some (.lit (.natVal (a - 1)))
   591    else if c = natAddName then some (.lit (.natVal (a + b)))
   592    else if c = natSubName then some (.lit (.natVal (a - b)))
   593    else if c = natMulName then some (.lit (.natVal (a * b)))
   594    else if c = natPowName then some (.lit (.natVal (a ^ b)))
   595    else if c = natDivName then some (.lit (.natVal (a / b)))
   596    else if c = natModName then some (.lit (.natVal (a % b)))
   597    else if c = natGcdName then some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.gcd a b)))
   598    else if c = natLandName then some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.land a b)))
   599    else if c = natLorName then some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.lor a b)))
   600    else if c = natXorName then some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.xor a b)))
   601    else if c = natShiftLeftName then
   602      some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.shiftLeft a b)))
   603    else if c = natShiftRightName then
   604      some (.lit (.natVal (Nat.shiftRight a b)))
   605    else if c = natBeqName then
   606      some (.const (if a = b then boolTrueName else boolFalseName) [])
   607    else if c = natBleName then
   608      some (.const (if a <= b then boolTrueName else boolFalseName) [])
   609    else none

== ConLeche/Kernel/CoreDefs.lean#L611-L638
   611  /-- Stored-constant guards for op `c`: the `Nat` basis, every
   612  dependency stored, and (for the `Bool`-valued ops and
   613  the `ble`-guarded `div`/`mod`, whose semantic clauses mention the
   614  `Bool` constructor values) the `Bool` constructors stored, level-free,
   615  at the type `Bool` itself (their values must be members of `Bool`'s,
   616  so that a recurrence `beq 0 0 = true` relates two members of one
   617  type).
   618  
   619  A dependency is only required to be stored: what kind of constant it
   620  is, its level parameters and its type are its own job's business.  At
   621  a certified operation's name nothing but a definition is accepted, and
   622  a definition there runs the operation's own install check, which pins
   623  its type (`natOpStoredOk`) and certifies its recurrences.  Storedness
   624  is what that leaves: an absent dependency would let a certificate pass
   625  over a name with nothing behind it. -/
   626  def natOpGuard (env : Env) (c : Name) : Bool :=
   627    natLitSupported env &&
   628    (natOpDeps c).all (fun n => (env.find? n).isSome) &&
   629    (if c = natBeqName || c = natBleName || natDivModNames.contains c then
   630      (match env.find? boolTrueName with
   631        | some ci => ci.toConstantVal.levelParams.isEmpty &&
   632            ci.toConstantVal.type == .const boolName []
   633        | none => false) &&
   634      (match env.find? boolFalseName with
   635        | some ci => ci.toConstantVal.levelParams.isEmpty &&
   636            ci.toConstantVal.type == .const boolName []
   637        | none => false)
   638     else true)

   669  def natOpCod (env : Env) (c : Name) (e : Expr) : Bool :=

   671      e == .const boolName [] &&
   672      (match env.find? boolName with
   673       | some ci => ci.toConstantVal.levelParams.isEmpty &&
   674           ci.toConstantVal.type == .sort (.succ .zero)
   675       | none => false)
   676    else e == .const natName []

   176        (preparePrelude pre ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra) := by

== ConLeche/SetTheory/Core.lean#L69-L172
    69  /-- A strictly first-order model of set theory of the strength the
    70  checker needs: membership, extensionality, pairing, union, power set,
    71  regularity, the first-order replacement schema, Jech-form choice, and
    72  an ω-chain of SGA4 Grothendieck universes. -/
    73  class SetTheory (V : Type u) where
    74    /-- Set membership. -/
    75    Mem : V → V → Prop
    76    /-- Extensionality: sets with the same members are equal. -/
    77    ext : ∀ {x y : V}, (∀ z, Mem z x ↔ Mem z y) → x = y
    78    /-- Pairing: the unordered pair. -/
    79    upair : V → V → V
    80    /-- Characterization of the unordered pair. -/
    81    mem_upair : ∀ {z a b : V}, Mem z (upair a b) ↔ z = a ∨ z = b
    82    /-- Union: the union of the members. -/
    83    sUnion : V → V
    84    /-- Characterization of the union. -/
    85    mem_sUnion : ∀ {z x : V}, Mem z (sUnion x) ↔ ∃ y, Mem y x ∧ Mem z y
    86    /-- Power set. -/
    87    power : V → V
    88    /-- Characterization of the power set: members are the subsets. -/
    89    mem_power : ∀ {z x : V}, Mem z (power x) ↔ ∀ w, Mem w z → Mem w x
    90    /-- Regularity: every nonempty set has an `∈`-minimal member. -/
    91    regularity : ∀ x : V, (∃ y, Mem y x) → ∃ y, Mem y x ∧ ¬ ∃ z, Mem z y ∧ Mem z x
    92    /-- First-order replacement schema: for any formula `φ` in `2 + p` free
    93    variables and parameters `params : Fin p → V`, if `φ` is functional on
    94    `a` (relating each `x ∈ a` to a unique `y`), the image exists as a set.
    95    Index `0` is `y` and index `1` is `x`, aligning with `DefFun 1`. -/
    96    replacement : ∀ {p : Nat} (φ : Formula (2 + p)) (params : Fin p → V) (a : V),
    97      (∀ x, Mem x a →
    98        ExistsUnique fun y => φ.eval Mem (fappend (fcons y (fcons x Fin.elim0)) params)) →
    99      ∃ b : V, ∀ z, Mem z b ↔
   100        ∃ x, Mem x a ∧ φ.eval Mem (fappend (fcons z (fcons x Fin.elim0)) params)
   101    /-- Axiom of Choice (Jech form): every set of nonempty sets admits a
   102    set-level choice function. -/
   103    choice : ∀ x : V, (∀ a, Mem a x → ∃ y, Mem y a) → ∃ f : V, IsChoiceFn Mem f x
   104    /-- An ω-chain of Grothendieck universes: the sets interpreting the
   105    universe tower (intended model `V_{κ n}`). -/
   106    univChain : Nat → V
   107    /-- The chain increases strictly: each universe is a member of the next. -/
   108    univChain_mem : ∀ n : Nat, Mem (univChain n) (univChain (n + 1))
   109    /-- Each chain member is a Grothendieck universe (`IsGrothendieck`). -/
   110    univChain_grothendieck : ∀ n : Nat, IsGrothendieck Mem (univChain n)
   111  
   112  namespace SetTheory
   113  
   114  @[inherit_doc] scoped infix:50 " ∈ˢ " => Mem
   115  
   116  variable {V : Type u} [SetTheory V]
   117  
   118  /-- Subset, from membership. -/
   119  protected def Subset (x y : V) : Prop := ∀ z, z ∈ˢ x → z ∈ˢ y
   120  
   121  @[inherit_doc] scoped infix:50 " ⊆ˢ " => SetTheory.Subset
   122  
   123  theorem Subset.refl (x : V) : x ⊆ˢ x := fun _ hz => hz
   124  
   125  theorem Subset.trans {x y z : V} (h₁ : x ⊆ˢ y) (h₂ : y ⊆ˢ z) : x ⊆ˢ z :=
   126    fun w hw => h₂ w (h₁ w hw)
   127  
   128  theorem Subset.antisymm {x y : V} (h₁ : x ⊆ˢ y) (h₂ : y ⊆ˢ x) : x = y :=
   129    ext fun z => ⟨h₁ z, h₂ z⟩
   130  
   131  theorem mem_power_iff_subset {z x : V} : z ∈ˢ power x ↔ z ⊆ˢ x := mem_power
   132  
   133  /-- Proof-carrying predicate asserting that the image `{f w : w ∈ a}`
   134  exists as a set in `V`. -/
   135  def HasImage (f : V → V) (a : V) : Prop :=
   136    ∃ b : V, ∀ z, z ∈ˢ b ↔ ∃ w, w ∈ˢ a ∧ z = f w
   137  
   138  /-- Proof-carrying, zero-junk replacement image `{f w : w ∈ a}`. -/
   139  noncomputable def image (f : V → V) (a : V) (h : HasImage f a) : V :=
   140    Classical.choose h
   141  
   142  theorem mem_image {f : V → V} {a z : V} {h : HasImage f a} :
   143      z ∈ˢ image f a h ↔ ∃ w, w ∈ˢ a ∧ z = f w :=
   144    Classical.choose_spec h z
   145  
   146  theorem HasImage.congr {a : V} {f g : V → V}
   147      (hfg : ∀ x, x ∈ˢ a → f x = g x) (hf : HasImage f a) : HasImage g a := by
   148    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hf
   149    refine ⟨b, fun z => (hb z).trans ?_⟩
   150    exact ⟨fun ⟨w, hw, hz⟩ => ⟨w, hw, hz.trans (hfg w hw)⟩,
   151           fun ⟨w, hw, hz⟩ => ⟨w, hw, hz.trans (hfg w hw).symm⟩⟩
   152  
   153  theorem HasImage.ext {a b : V} {f g : V → V} (hab : a = b)
   154      (hfg : ∀ x, x ∈ˢ a → f x = g x) (hf : HasImage f a) : HasImage g b :=
   155    hab ▸ hf.congr hfg
   156  
   157  theorem image_congr {a : V} {f g : V → V} (hf : HasImage f a) (hg : HasImage g a)
   158      (h : ∀ x, x ∈ˢ a → f x = g x) : image f a hf = image g a hg :=
   159    ext fun z => by
   160      rw [mem_image (h := hf), mem_image (h := hg)]
   161      exact ⟨fun ⟨w, hw, hz⟩ => ⟨w, hw, hz.trans (h w hw)⟩,
   162             fun ⟨w, hw, hz⟩ => ⟨w, hw, hz.trans (h w hw).symm⟩⟩
   163  
   164  theorem image_ext {a b : V} {f g : V → V} (hab : a = b)
   165      (hf : HasImage f a) (hg : HasImage g b)
   166      (h : ∀ x, x ∈ˢ a → f x = g x) : image f a hf = image g b hg := by
   167    subst hab
   168    exact image_congr hf hg h
   169  
   170  attribute [irreducible] image
   171  
   172  end SetTheory

== ConLeche/SetTheory/Core.lean#L56-L67
    56  structure IsGrothendieck {V : Type u} (Mem : V → V → Prop) (u : V) : Prop where
    57    /-- *Transitivity*: members of members are members. -/
    58    transitivity : ∀ y z, Mem y u → Mem z y → Mem z u
    59    /-- *Pairing*: unordered pairs of members are members. -/
    60    pairing : ∀ a b, Mem a u → Mem b u → ∃ p, Mem p u ∧ IsUpair Mem p a b
    61    /-- *Power sets*: power sets of members are members. -/
    62    powerSet : ∀ y, Mem y u → ∃ p, Mem p u ∧ ∀ z, Mem z p ↔ ∀ w, Mem w z → Mem w y
    63    /-- *Indexed union*: the union of the range of any internal function graph
    64    `g : I → u` with `I ∈ u` is a member of `u`. -/
    65    indexedUnion : ∀ I g, Mem I u → IsFunGraph Mem g I u →
    66      ∃ w, Mem w u ∧ ∀ z, Mem z w ↔
    67        ∃ i y p, Mem i I ∧ Mem y u ∧ Mem p g ∧ IsKPair Mem p i y ∧ Mem z y

== ConLeche/SetTheory/Core.lean#L174-L188
   174  /-- **Model existence (consistency / non-vacuity assumption).**
   175  There exists a model `(V, SetTheory V)` of our strictly first-order set theory
   176  (`ZFC⁻` + an ω-chain of SGA4 Grothendieck universes).
   177  
   178  Because `SetTheory` is strictly first-order (`Formula`, `IsGrothendieck`,
   179  Jech-form `choice`), model existence is essentially the consistency of this
   180  set theory: classically, by Gödel's completeness theorem, a first-order theory
   181  has a model iff it is syntactically consistent (and by downward
   182  Löwenheim–Skolem already at `Type 0`).  The `*_no_False` theorems take
   183  `ModelExists` explicitly — rather than an unused `(V : Type w) [SetTheory V]`
   184  parameter — because we need the background set theory to be non-vacuous
   185  (consistent) for those theorems to be meaningful. -/
   186  def ModelExists : Prop :=
   187    Nonempty (Σ V : Type u, SetTheory V)
   188

== ConLeche/Kernel/TrustAxioms.lean#L9-L38
     9  /-!
    10  # The compiler-trust axiom family (task #95)
    11  
    12  `Init`'s compiler-trust scaffolding is installed rather than
    13  declined:
    14  
    15  * `Lean.trustCompiler : True` is trivially realizable — it is
    16    installed as an *opaque* (stored `axiomInfo`, exactly like a checked
    17    `opaque` declaration) with value `True.intro`, over a pinned `True`
    18    family.  No new meta-axiom: the model is `True.intro`'s own
    19    interpretation.
    20  * `Lean.reduceNat` / `Lean.reduceBool` then check as ordinary
    21    `opaque`s (their exported values are identity functions modulo the
    22    `have := trustCompiler` wrapper); at its check their stored values are
    23    pinned against the identity function
    24    (`ConLeche/Kernel/TrustPins.lean`, hand-pinned since task #273 —
    25    every toolchain's definition after zeta) by definitional equality —
    26    the task-#47 pattern: drift declines, never silently.
    27  * `Lean.ofReduceNat` / `Lean.ofReduceBool` are pinned axioms over
    28    those stored opaques (the task-#34 standard-axioms machinery).  With
    29    the stored reduce operation certified to be the identity (a
    30    definitional-equality certificate at the operation's own install,
    31    `checkReducePin`; the axiom's install checks `ofReduceAxOk`),
    32    `∀ a b, reduceNat a = b → a = b` interprets to
    33    an inhabited proposition (the hypothesis *is* the conclusion), so
    34    both axioms are true in the set model with the proof point as value.
    35  
    36  `sorryAx` remains the only axiom tolerated as a *declaration*: its
    37  record installs nothing and any use of it declines
    38  (`sorryAxName`, `ConLeche/Kernel/Basis/Names.lean`).

== ConLeche/OleanInput.lean#L97-L98
    97  def Sees (sp : Roots) (fs : FS) (m n m' : Name) : Prop :=
    98    ∃ p c, Loads sp fs m m' p ∧ InModulePart sp fs m' p c ∧ c.name = n

== ConLeche/Frontend/Olean/Snapshot.lean#L52-L66
    52  inductive LoadsAt (sp : Roots) (fs : FS) (g : Bool) (imps0 : Array ImportRec) : Name → Bool → Prop
    53    | root {i : ImportRec} : i ∈ imps0 → LoadsAt sp fs g imps0 i.module (g || i.importAll)
    54    | step {a : Name} {all : Bool} {d : ModDecoded} {i : ImportRec} :
    55        LoadsAt sp fs g imps0 a all → ViewOf sp fs a d → i ∈ d.imports →
    56        (i.isExported || all) = true → LoadsAt sp fs g imps0 i.module (g || all && i.importAll)
    57  
    58  /-- **Module `m`'s header loads part `p` of `m'`**: the private part where some path loads it
    59  whole, else the exported part (`LoadsAt`, from `m`'s private view's header). -/
    60  def Loads (sp : Roots) (fs : FS) (m m' : Name) (p : OLeanLevel) : Prop :=
    61    ∃ d, ViewOf sp fs m d ∧
    62      match p with
    63      | .private => LoadsAt sp fs (!d.isModule) d.imports m' true
    64      | .exported => LoadsAt sp fs (!d.isModule) d.imports m' false ∧
    65          ¬ LoadsAt sp fs (!d.isModule) d.imports m' true
    66      | .server => False
